items.title: Tova Davidson, Executive Director, Sustainable Waterloo Region
notes:
Tova Davidson, Executive Director, Sustainable Waterloo Region appeared before the Committee to speak in support of bringing the LRT into Cambridge and the Ainslie Street terminal. T. Davidson noted that bringing the LRT to downtown Cambridge will bring prosperity, and good connections, resulting in a simpler and more comfortable way of travelling. T. Davidson also reminded the Committee that this is well aligned with the transformWR strategy in encouraging active and public transportation, as half of our local carbon footprint comes from transportation alone. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, T. Davidson noted that it would be beneficial to have guidelines for accessible and sustainable housing, to ensure that all areas around the LRT are accessible and that exclusive high income areas are not being created, pushing others out.

items.title: Dan Clements, Citizens for Cambridge
notes: Dan Clements appeared before the Committee on behalf of the Citizens for Cambridge to share their support for the LRT staff recommendation and to urge Council to support the recommendation without delay. D. Clements noted benefits of the Ainslie Street terminal include its close proximity to Main Street, support for Galt's core businesses, easy walking distance to the gaslight district and the inherit connection to buses and other transportation.

items.title: Brian Kennedy, Executive Director, Downtown Cambridge Business Improvement Association
notes: Brian Kennedy appeared before the Committee on behalf of the Downtown Cambridge BIA to share their support for the staff recommendation and to thank staff and Council for their concerted efforts on this item. B. Kennedy noted that Stage 2 ION is a crucial investment as it stimulates economic growth, supports affordable housing efforts, access to public services and better connectivity throughout the Region.

items.title: Mackenzie Meek, Planner/Project Manager, Cambridge Mill
notes: Mackenzie Meek, Planner/Project Manager, Cambridge Mill appeared before the Committee to share their support for the staff recommendation. M. Meek noted that the Cambridge LRT is not just a want, but a need and that it aligns seamlessly with the Region's strategic plan. M. Meek stated that the LRT is not just a transportation solution, but an investment into the future of Cambridge.

items.title: Nathan Whalen, Cambridge
notes:
Nathan Whalen appeared before the Committee to ask that staff integrate the planning of a Cambridge GO train station with the LRT planning and construction. 

A copy of their presentation is attached to the minutes. 

Responding to questions from the Committee, Mathieu Goetzke, Commissioner Transportation Services shared that the study on the preliminary GO train design between Cambridge and Guelph is already underway, with plans for staff to bring back a report to Council in Spring 2024. M. Goetzke cautioned on tying the GO train too tightly with the LRT, as the Cambridge GO connection is still in an earlier stage and would not want it to delay Stage 2 LRT.

items.title: TSD-RTS-23-004, Stage 2 ION South Terminal Preferred Location (Staff Presentation)
notes:
Matthew O'Neil, Manager, Rapid Transit Coordination provided a presentation that gave an overview of the evaluation criteria and results, and a summary of next steps, which included a schedule for the terminal design and business case. 

A copy of the presentation is attached to the minutes. 

M. Harris joined the meeting at 9:55 am.

Responding to questions from the Committee, M. O'Neil shared that the LRT and Cambridge GO station are both great projects that are being advanced independently, but that they are compatible. M. Goetzke noted that a report will be coming to the Committee in Spring 2024 regarding the feasibility of the Cambridge GO train station and staff can bring Council the option of acquiring land as part of that project. 

The Committee directed staff to return in Spring 2024 with a report on the Cambridge GO train station, which includes land acquisition options. 

Responding to a question from the Committee, Graham Walsh, Regional Solicitor, confirmed that development charges collected specifically to fund GO stations can be used for the construction costs and that some costs, such as land acquisition, are excluded. 

In response to a question from the Committee, R. Regier stated that staff are well positioned to leverage the experiences from LRT Stage 1 and to build from those experiences for Stage 2, in order to meet the needs of the community. M. Goetzke shared that staff have been starting to strengthen competencies around transportation equity and building partnerships to fuse those competencies within the business case methodology and study.

motions.item_title: PDL-CPL-23-032, Memoranda of Understanding between the Region of Waterloo and Grand River Conservation Authority for Non-Mandatory Services and Programs
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services to enter into a Memoranda of Understanding with the Grand River Conservation Authority for Non-Mandatory Services and Programs in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as outlined in Report PDL-CPL-23-032, dated December 5, 2023. That the Regional Clerk circulate this report to the Minister of Natural Resources and Forestry, Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing, the area municipalities, and the Grand River Conservation Authority.

That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development, and Legislative Services to enter into a Memoranda of Understanding with the Grand River Conservation Authority for Non-Mandatory Services and Programs in a form satisfactory to the Regional Solicitor, as outlined in Report PDL-CPL-23-032, dated December 5, 2023.

motions.item_title: PDL-CPL-23-035, Brownfields Financial Incentive Program - Tax Increment Grant - 201 and 217 Hespeler Road, Cambridge
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 201 and 217 Hespeler Rd in the City of Cambridge, as described in Report PDL-CPL-23-035 dated December 5, 2023: Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant (TIG) with the Regional amount not to exceed $1,299,598, net of any future brownfield assistance, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements with the registered owner of 201 and 217 Hespeler Road and the City of Cambridge, with the form and content of such agreement(s) to be satisfactory to both the Regional and City of Cambridge Solicitors.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following actions regarding the property municipally known as 201 and 217 Hespeler Rd in the City of Cambridge, as described in Report PDL-CPL-23-035 dated December 5, 2023:

  1. Approve a joint Tax Increment Grant (TIG) with the Regional amount not to exceed $1,299,598, net of any future brownfield assistance, to be financed from the incremental tax revenue for the property following remediation, redevelopment and reassessment; and
  2. Authorize the Region’s Commissioner of Planning, Development and Legislative Services and Commissioner, Corporate Services / Chief Financial Officer to execute any associated agreements with the registered owner of 201 and 217 Hespeler Road and the City of Cambridge, with the form and content of such agreement(s) to be satisfactory to both the Regional and City of Cambridge Solicitors.

motions.item_title: TSD-RTS-23-004, Stage 2 ION South Terminal Preferred Location (Staff Presentation)
motions.text: That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo endorse location T1, as outlined in Attachment A of report TSD-RTS-23-004, dated December 5, 2023 as the preferred Stage 2 ION south terminal location, and direct staff to proceed with only location T1 in the initial business case (IBC).
